title: Define deterministic routing priority DAG for pinned versions, region/tier selection and canary/A-B rollouts
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem: Interactions between model version pinning, region and tier-based routing, and canary/A-B rollouts produce nondeterministic behavior in edge cases (session pins, API key-level pins, and prefix cache reuse). This ticket defines a single deterministic priority DAG, explicit tie-break rules, and a small policy extension to support 'pin_override' and 'pin_scoped' behaviors so product teams can express intent without surprising fallthrough behavior.

Goals:
- Make routing decisions deterministic and explainable to customers.
- Preserve SLA guarantees for Dedicated/Reserved customers while enabling gradual rollouts.
- Ensure KV cache and prefix-caching remain compatible when traffic is redirected to different model variants.

Scope: design policy, implement router ordering, add unit/integration tests, update console docs and rollout UI. Not in scope: changes to kernel selection heuristics or quantization profiles (handled elsewhere).
user_story: As an engineer operating model rollouts, I want a predictable order of routing precedence so that pinned sessions and enterprise contracts are never silently routed to a canary variant unless explicitly allowed.
decision_record: Adopt a clear routing priority DAG: 1) Explicit session pin > 2) Account-level pin > 3) Route-level pin > 4) Region/tier constraints > 5) Canary/A-B weights > 6) Fallback variant mapping.
Introduce two new optional flags on pins: 'pin_override' (pin wins even if rollout would route elsewhere) and 'pin_scoped' (pin applies only within the same model family; fallback allowed otherwise).

When a pinned model is unavailable in the selected region/tier, follow 'pin_scoped' semantics: if pin_scoped=true, allow fallback to model variant in same family; if false, honor pin by returning a controlled 503 with a descriptive error for enterprise customers (fail-closed).

Canary weights are evaluated only after pins and region/tier filters reduce the candidate set. Canary assignment must be based on stable hashing of request id + account id to avoid churn and keep canary session stickiness.

KV cache compatibility: router will prefer variants with equal or compatible kv_schema versions. If a canary variant is incompatible, it will not be selected for requests that present an existing KV cache token unless 'force_migrate' policy is enabled on the route.
acceptance_criteria: Routing decision engine implements the priority DAG and produces deterministic decisions for 1000 randomized test cases (seeded) including session pins, account pins, and canary weights.
Unit tests cover pin_override=true/false semantics, pin_scoped behavior, and the case where pinned model lacks regional availability.
Integration tests demonstrate KV cache safety by rejecting incompatible variant selection unless force_migrate=true and a migration path is exercised.
Console UI surfaces the effective routing decision: show which rule matched (pin, region filter, canary), and for pinned requests expose the pin source (session/account/route).
Docs updated: runtime routing docs and API contract updated with examples and error messages for controlled fail-closed behavior.
implementation_notes: Add RoutingDecision struct with provenance tags (source: session_pin|account_pin|route_pin|region_filter|canary|fallback) and deterministic score used only for tie-breaking.
Stable hashing: use xxhash64(request_id || account_id || route_id) % 10000 to assign canary buckets. Store mapping for session stickiness for 24h by default.
Region/tier prefilter: evaluate region availability first to reduce candidate set (saves kernel selection/latency).
Expose 'pin_override' and 'pin_scoped' on the pin API and internal pin config. Default pin_override=false, pin_scoped=false to preserve current conservative behavior.
Telemetry: emit routing.trace events with candidate set, chosen variant, and reason to aid post-rollout debugging and alerting.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Enterprise customers with pins may experience 503s if pinned model is not available in region. Mitigation: add preflight validation in Console when creating pins, and recommend pin_scoped=true for cross-region resiliency.
Risk: Canary stickiness increases traffic skew during autoscaling. Mitigation: cap per-instance canary percent and monitor throughput; provide emergency toggle to revert to pre-rollout routing.
Risk: KV cache migration could regress latency. Mitigation: require force_migrate opt-in and provide a staged migration plan with sampling.
testing_plan: Unit tests for RoutingDecision ordering and tie-breaks (ENG routing repo).
Integration tests: synthetic traffic simulating 10k requests across regions and pinned/account scenarios; verify no unexpected deviations from DAG.
E2E canary: rollout to internal org (redwood-infra) at 5% traffic, observe telemetry and KV cache hit-rate for 48h, then expand to 25% and 100% with monitoring gates.
Load test with Dedicated pools to assert latency SLOs unaffected by new routing overhead.
